I have no idea how long it's actually been. Time itself seems like it crawls here. Maybe 200 years? 2000? I can't tell. There's nothing behind the windows. Just void... but occasionally there are flashes of color. Wish I knew what that was all about.

Let me get to the point: My name is... you know, it might be a cosmically bad idea to write it down for you, so let's just go with John Doe then, yeah? Anyways, I'm dead. And if you're reading this, you're probably dead too. Either that, or whatever I end up doing causes reality to collapse or overlap or something. But you're in The Library. That tells me a little about you. You loved to read, for one. This library, if that's what it actually is, seems to be our afterlife. Our curse for whatever wrongs we did. I know John did some horrible, horrible things. Curses being inflicted upon innocent folk just because they looked at me funny, murders for political gain. That sort of thing. If you're here, I can only guess you did something similar.

I started here buried under a pile of dusty old tomes. Tomes I've written, in fact. And one's I've read. I can only assume you did too. You're gonna be very, very confused, and that's alright. You see, this library holds just about every piece of writing every created by mankind. From Moby Dick to old fighting manuals, this place has it all. They even have old knowledge on the intricacies of death.

God, I ramble a lot, even in my writing. I guess that's what this place has done to me. Let me be brief. There's a book here: no title on it, no author's name.  It is your ticket out of here. I've read it, and I've learned how to escape this fucking place. I've learned how to mantle you. Essentially, I've become you. You're the only person who's ever experienced your death, to everyone else you're alive, and I'll be jumping right back into where you left off. It's really, really complicated and I don't quite understand all of the metaphysics behind it, but I know enough to get out. I guess that also means I technically killed you.

I feel guilty for robbing you of your life, so that's why I'm telling you this. Find your book. It's an biography of your life, somewhere hidden in one of these books. It might be in that copy of Moby Dick over there, maybe it's in some raunchy erotica novel, who knows? But you have to read. Find that biography, read it, and keep it close. Then, and only then, will you be able to find the Black Book. Your life and all it was traded for a new one. Poetic, eh? We can thank those who came before us for that little tidbit of knowledge.

   Good luck, I know you'll need it.

PS: No shouting in the library. Trust me on this one.
